item.title: Venezuela Ships First Crude Cargo to Israel as Oil Exports Reopen After Maduro’s Ouster
item.description: Venezuela is sending its first crude oil cargo to Israel in years as the Latin American country’s exports open up following the capture of its president Nicolas Maduro.

item.title: Trump Tariffs Face Rebuke as Johnson Fails to Block Votes
item.description: House lawmakers could vote as soon as Wednesday on whether to reject some of President Donald Trump’s tariff policies, ahead of a midterm election focused heavily on anxiety over the US cost of living.

item.title: Urban Migration in India Sets Stage for Record Property IPO Year
item.description: India’s real estate developers are turning to capital markets to raise funds, signaling their confidence that the shift of millions of people toward cities will ensure robust demand.

item.title: Netanyahu, in Hasty Trip, to Warn Trump Against Narrow Iran Deal
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu is set to meet Donald Trump in the White House on Wednesday as Israel’s concerns over a potential diplomatic deal between Iran and the US mount.

item.title: Power Engineering Firm Solv Energy Raises $512.5 Million in IPO
item.description: Solv Energy Inc. raised $512.5 million in a US initial public offering, pricing its shares at the top of the marketed range.

item.title: US Changes India Trade Deal Statement, Sparking Confusion
item.description: The White House revised its fact sheet on the US-India trade agreement to adjust language around agricultural goods, adding to confusion about the deal already raised by farmer groups.

item.title: Upended World Is Pushing EU to Finish Single Market, Costa Says
item.description: European Union leaders are finally ready to unify their markets to compete globally, European Council President Antonio Costa said, arguing that the fracturing world order is driving the continent to act.
